title: Fix: Deploy to shinyapps.io fails due to archived CRAN packages
description:
## Problem

The \"Deploy to shinyapps.io\" CI job fails on every push to `main` because `pak` cannot resolve four packages that have been archived or removed from CRAN:

- `biclust`
- `metricsgraphics`
- `rbokeh`
- `maptools`

Error from CI ([run 27718742742](https://github.com/rstudio/flexdashboard/actions/runs/27718742742)):

```
* Can't install dependency metricsgraphics
* Can't install dependency rbokeh
* Can't install dependency maptools
* biclust: Can't find package called biclust, metricsgraphics, rbokeh, maptools.
```

## Affected examples

| Example | Package |
|---|---|
| `examples/03_shiny-biclust/` | `biclust` |
| `examples/09_rbokeh/` | `rbokeh` |
| `examples/10_metricsgraphics-tor/` | `metricsgraphics` |
| `examples/07_storyboard/` | `metricsgraphics` |
| `examples/12_leaflet-waste/` | `maptools` |

## Suggested fix

Three of the four packages are available on GitHub and can likely be installed from there:

- `biclust` → `Biclustering/biclust`
- `rbokeh` → `hafen/rbokeh`
- `metricsgraphics` → `hrbrmstr/metricsgraphics`

`maptools` was formally retired from CRAN in October 2023 (part of the sp/rgeos ecosystem retirement). There is no maintained GitHub source. The `12_leaflet-waste` example that depends on it may need to be updated to remove the `maptools` dependency, or removed from the deploy list.

The `extra-packages` field in the workflow's `setup-r-package` step (in `.github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml`) and/or a `DESCRIPTION`-level `Remotes:` field would be the right place to wire up the GitHub installs.

title: bslib::tooltip not displaying in flexdashboard
description:
Hello,
I'm trying to add some additional information to my flexdashboard app.  Looks like the tooltip message does not show up in flexdashboard while it shows up in a "regular" shiny app (see reprex below). 
Could any one assist me with this issue?

Flexdashboard code

```` r
---
  title: "bslib::tooltip-test"
output: flexdashboard::flex_dashboard
runtime: shiny
---
  
  ```{r}
library(shiny)
library(bslib)
library(bsicons)
```

```{r}
span(
  "Some text",
  tooltip(
    bs_icon("info-circle"),
    "Tooltip message",
    placement = "right"
  )
)
```
````
Shiny code

``` r
library(shiny)
library(bslib)
library(bsicons)

ui <- page_fillable(
  span(
    "Some text",
    tooltip(
      bs_icon("info-circle"),
      "Tooltip message",
      placement = "right"
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

title: Broken Shiny table formatting when viewed in flexdashboard
description:
I have a simple table that is rendered correctly as a Shiny app, but becomes broken when embedded into flexdashboard.

Here is what it looks like as a native Shiny app:

![t1](https://github.com/rstudio/flexdashboard/assets/142856165/1d504abb-41cb-48b9-bba6-8802c39c62b6)

But this happens when its embedded into flexdashboard:

![t2](https://github.com/rstudio/flexdashboard/assets/142856165/58e0ffe0-cccb-4e5b-997f-cc8a30f5a410)

This bug is easy to reproduce.  The following native Shiny app code is put into `bug_test.R`:
```
library(DT)
library(shiny)

ui_test <- fluidPage(
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(),
    mainPanel(
      DT::dataTableOutput("table"),
    )
  )
)

server_test <- function(input, output) {

  output$table <- DT::renderDataTable(DT::datatable({
    colA <- c("A", "B", "C")
    colB <- c("X", "Y", "Z")
    colC <- c("1", "2", "3")
    return(data.frame(colA, colB, colC))
  }), options = list(
    dom = "t",
    ordering = FALSE,
    autoWidth = TRUE,
    columnDefs = list(
      list(className = "dt-right", targets = 1),
      list(width = "150px", targets = 0),
      list(width = "200px", targets = 1),
      list(width = "100px", targets = 2)
    )
  ), selection = "none", rownames = FALSE, escape = FALSE)

}

shinyApp(ui = ui_test, server = server_test)
```

The flexdashboard code (`test.Rmd`) is:
````
---
title: "Test"
output: 
  flexdashboard::flex_dashboard:
    orientation: rows
    vertical_layout: scroll
runtime: shiny
---
Tab Name
=======================================================================

```{r}
source("bug_test.R")

shinyApp(ui = ui_test, server = server_test)
```
````

I am using the latest version of RStudio (2024.04.2, Build 764), and the latest versions of all modules (Shiny 1.8.1.1, DT 0.33, flexdashboard 0.6.2).

title: Compatibility with Plausible analytics
description:
Thank you for the great package; flexdashboard powers an R-Ladies YouTube [dashboard](https://ivelasq.github.io/rladies-video-feed) that @ivelasq and I created and featured in her [blog](https://ivelasq.rbind.io/blog/automated-youtube-dashboard). We recently added Plausible analytics to the dashboard and noticed that the answer to a related issue provided [here](https://github.com/rstudio/flexdashboard/issues/243#issuecomment-1448923919) doesn't work for Plausible:

```yaml
---
title: ""
output: 
  flexdashboard::flex_dashboard:
    includes:
      in_header: plausible.html
---
```

 The reason is because Plausible requires their analytics script to be added to the header verbatim, however during the `rmarkdown::render()` process a malformed script is added to the header when using the YAML above.

The reprexes below show the following:
1. Current flexdashboard behavior with `includes:` followed by `in_header:`: a malformed script is added to the header.
2. Current flexdashboard behavior with `pandoc_args:` followed by `include-in-header:`: a malformed script is added to the body. It's unclear to me why this adds the script so far down the page.
3. Desired flexdashboard behavior requested in this issue: I added the Plausible script verbatim by modifying the rendered dashboard .html using the shell command `sed`. This could be implemented in flexdashboard in a way that retains the old behavior when files are passed to `includes:`, by adding an option for direct text input that interpolates text verbatim into the rendered .html (see 4. below).
4. pkgdown has already [implemented](https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/pull/1852/files#diff-67de5b43c1a21eec46f47326878d9c64a9a2f8795b6780c3a7357d149ed957ea) the desired behavior in https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/pull/1852 using the whisker R package and mustache templates. In this case, only direct text input can be passed to the pkgdown template (files cannot be passed).

library(flexdashboard)
library(fs)
library(glue)
library(pkgdown)
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(rmarkdown))
library(usethis)

find_script <- function(path) {
  grep("plausible", readLines(path))
}

src <- "https://plausible.io/js/script.js"
script <- glue('<script defer data-domain="{dom}" src="{src}"></script>')
cat(script, file = "./plausible.html", sep = "\n")

yaml1_part2 <- '    includes:\n      in_header: plausible.html\n---'

title: Notes are silently dropped if a no-output producing chunk is inserted
description:
## Disclaimer

I previously [asked this question on SO](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/77887360/chart-notes-are-not-shown-in-flexdashboard-if-an-empty-chunk-is-added-at-the-end) to check whether this behavior is maybe intentional and got a workaround as a solution, but I am still not sure whether this behavior is really intentional.

## Problem

When adding a chunk, which produces no output (for example to close a database connection), after a chunk with notes, the notes ( added via `>`) disappear.

## Reprex

``````
---

description:
source: [Output flexdashboard with renderLeaflet to html](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/76972645/output-flexdashboard-with-renderleaflet-to-html)


I have flexdashboard code that works when I run it within RStudio (using the "Run Document" button and viewing in RStudio's viewer - and also when clicking the "Open in Browser" button in viewer, it opens a system browser and works fine). However, if I use `rmarkdown::render()` to output it to an html file, the reactive leaflet maps no longer work and are blank. The maps that are output using `leaflet()` work, but not `renderLeaflet()`.


for example:

```
---
title: "Project Dashboard"
output:
flexdashboard::flex_dashboard:
orientation: columns
runtime: shiny
---

```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(leaflet)
library(flexdashboard)

```

```{r data}
# Create the data
cities_data <- data.frame(
  Name = c("City A", "City B", "City C"),

  Longitude = c(-74.0060, -118.2437, -0.1278)

  st_set_crs(4326)
```

```

```{r}

    addCircleMarkers(data = cities_data %>% filter(Name == input$Name),

title: Navigation bar obscuring content
description:
When designing a flexdashboard with multiple pages (each with long titles), the navigation bar at the top fills up rapidly. With all but the largest screen sizes, it splits into two or more lines, which then obscure the text beneath.

Several solutions have been discussed on other channels:

- Adding lots of blank lines between the navigation bar and contents is suggested [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/42914936/prevent-navigation-bar-from-overlapping-content-in-flexdashboard-r). This isn't ideal – as on a wider screen (when the navbar is still on one line), there's then a very obvious gap between the navbar and the page content. 
- Putting the tabs in drop down menus is also (discussed [there](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/42914936/prevent-navigation-bar-from-overlapping-content-in-flexdashboard-r)), but won't always be appropriate (depending on the structure of the dashboard)
- Using media queries and fiddling around with divs (suggested on stackoverflow [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/67941461/navbar-in-r-flexdashboard-cuts-off-main-content?noredirect=1&lq=1) and explained in more detail [here](https://www.w3schools.com/css/tryit.asp?filename=trycss_mediaqueries_hide)) feels like a very long-winded way of going about this… so I feel there must be a better way!
- I also recently posted about this on the [Posit community](https://community.rstudio.com/t/navigation-bar-obscuring-content-in-flexdashboard/156257)

It seems that this would be a very useful addition to the flexdashboard package - detecting when the screen size and navigation bar length are such that the navbar spills onto 2 or more lines, then moving the content down on the page automatically so it isn't overlapped by the navbar.

This could always be added as an optional feature (turned on or off in YAML) for those who for whatever reason don't want it.

Please could you consider adding this feature to your next update? 

Thanks very much in advance for your help - it’s a great package otherwise! :)

title: Way to tell init javascript to ignore contents of div?
description:
I have an app that writes rendered rmarkdown (as HTML) into a shiny uiOutput. This HTML contains tags that the flexdashboard init javascript uses to structure the page (e.g. divs of class "section level2") just because of how it is rendered. Normally, this is not a problem, because the content is filled by shiny AFTER the init script is run, which means it renders as intended. I'm now trying to build a "static" (non-shiny) version of the same page. Consider the following script: ```` --- title: "Untitled" output: flexdashboard::flex_dashboard: orientation: columns vertical_layout: fill --- ```{r setup, include=FALSE} library(flexdashboard) ``` Column {.sidebar} ----------------------------------------------------------------------- ### Sidebar sidebar Column ----------------------------------------------------------------------- ### Chart B Top ### Chart C ```{r} h = '
text0
text1
text2
text3
text4' htmltools::tags$div(htmltools::HTML(h)) ``` ```` When this is compiled, the flexdashboard init script screws up the page format (I think) because it sees the `level1`, `level2`, etc divs in `h` as things to be moved around. I do not want flexdashboard to mess with that html. Is there a way to achieve this? Things I've tried: * iframe: doesn't work because I want the HTML to be styled using the parent page's css * javascript: I've tried passing the html as a base64 encoded string, which is then decoded and put into the appropriate div. I know this works if I can delay this until AFTER the flexdashboard init runs. However, I don't have an elegant way of doing this. If I inlcude the decoding script in a script tag to run on document ready, it gets run before the init by default (I guess it is queued up first?). I can use setTimeout() to delay the content replacement until after the flexdashboard init, but this is very inelegant (and potentially error-prone). Is there a class I can set on the containing div can set to make flexdashboard init ignore the contents? Or a way to queue up my decoding script to run immediately after flexdashboard init? Thanks!

title: No reference to spaces as special characters in page attributes
description:
Spaces in page attributes (a.k.a. class attributes) fail silently while knitting. I can't find any references that mention that spaces are special characters in page attributes or that spaces should not be included before or after the equal sign in page attributes. I think this issue is specific to flexdashboard rather than e.g. RMarkdown or knitr because it's related to flexdashboard documentation. Does this documentation exist and, if so, could it be more apparent?

Other related questions include: 
- [Flexdashboard multiple attributes page](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/47712019/flexdashboard-multiple-attributes-page); multiple attributes are needed but there's no reference stating how the attributes should be delimited.

Related references include:
- [RMarkdown - Attributes on Sections](https://bookdown.org/yihui/rmarkdown/layout.html#attributes-on-sections)
- [Flexdashboard - Page Navigation](https://rstudio.github.io/flexdashboard/articles/using.html#page-navigation-1)

# MWE
```
---
title: "Page Navigation Menus"
output: flexdashboard::flex_dashboard
---

Page 1 {data-navmenu="Menu A"}
=====================================


Page 2 {data-navmenu= "Menu A"} <!-- page attribute contains a space and fails silently -->
=====================================  


Page 3 {data-navmenu="Menu B"}
=====================================


Page 4 {data-navmenu="Menu B"}
===================================== 
 ```

title: Critical and High Vulnerabilities
description:
We are using flexdashboard in a containerized data pipeline and recently have seen that the container scan (Trivy v0.17.2) started reporting the following vulnerabilities:

- CVE-2021-23440 (critical)
- CVE-2021-3807 (high)
- CVE-2020-28469 (high)
- CVE-2021-3803 (high)

The vulnerabilities go away as soon as we remove flexdashboard.  The container is built up using rocker/r-ver:4.1.1 as a starting point.  These vulnerabilities indicate that flexdashboard uses what appear to be pretty old npm packages (a couple of major versions older than the latest).

I first noticed this while installing the pkg from https://packagemanager.rstudio.com/all/__linux__/focal/latest/src/contrib/flexdashboard_0.5.2.tar.gz', but also got the same vulnerabilities detected by our DTR when I installed it from github using devtools.

Are there plans to update flexdashboard to address these vulnerabilities?  I am not a node person so I don't fully grasp how much work this would be, but I would gladly test any updated versions that may come out of this.

Thank you!  Marcelo

Cc @schloerke

The `master` branch of this repository will soon be renamed to `main`, as part of a coordinated change across several GitHub organizations (including, but not limited to: [tidyverse](https://github.com/tidyverse), [r-lib](https://github.com/r-lib), [tidymodels](https://github.com/tidymodels), and [sol-eng](https://github.com/sol-eng)). We anticipate this will happen by the end of September 2021.

That will be preceded by a release of the [usethis package](https://usethis.r-lib.org), which will gain some functionality around detecting and adapting to a renamed default branch. There will also be a blog post at the time of this `master` --> `main` change.

The purpose of this issue is to:

* Help us firm up the list of targetted repositories
* Make sure all maintainers are aware of what's coming
* Give us an issue to close when the job is done
* Give us a place to put advice for collaborators re: how to adapt

description:
I would like the gauge label to change when the value changes.

I created the `f_3` function to try to adjust this, but not succeed.

 `rmarkdown` code:

    ---
    title: "Label of gauge"
    runtime: shiny
    output: 
      flexdashboard::flex_dashboard:
        orientation: rows
        vertical_layout: fill
        theme: yeti
    ---

    side{.sidebar}
    -------------------------------------------

    ```{r}
    library(tibble)
    library(shiny)
    library(shinyWidgets)
    library(flexdashboard)
    ```

    **Analysis**

    ```{r}
    autonumericInput(
        inputId = "a", 
        value = 10, 
        label = "Value 1", 
        align = "center", 
        currencySymbol = "$", 
        currencySymbolPlacement = "p",
        digitGroupSeparator = ".",
        decimalCharacter = ",", 
        decimalPlaces = 0, 
        minimumValue = 0, 
        maximumValue = 100
    )

    autonumericInput(
        inputId = "b", 
        value = 10, 
        label = "Value 2", 
        align = "center", 
        currencySymbol = "R$", 
        currencySymbolPlacement = "p", 
        digitGroupSeparator = ".",
        decimalCharacter = ",", 
        decimalPlaces = 0, 
        minimumValue = 0, 
        maximumValue = 100
        )
    ```

    ```{r}
    f_1 <- function(a, b) {
      a + b
    }

    reac <- reactive({
      tibble(
        a = input$a, 
        b = input$b
      )
    })

    pred <- reactive({
      temp <- reac()
      f_1(
        a = input$a, 
        b = input$b
      )
    })
    ```

    abc{}
    --------------------------------------

    ###
    ```{r}
    f_3 <- function(x) {
      if (x <= 40) {
        "Danger"
      } else if (x <= 80) {
        "Warning"
      } else ("Success")
    }

    renderGauge({
      gauge(
        value = round(x = pred(), digits = 0), min = 0, max = 100, symbol = "%", 
        label = f_3(x = pred())
        )
    })
    ```
The label's value always appears as `Danger`, even when the value changes. 

This question was answered [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/69013336/how-change-flexdashbordgauges-label-in-shiny-application-with-reactive-data/69021155#69021155), I just wanted to know why this happened? Was it a bug?

title: Documentation for theme argument in flex_dashboard does not describe how to pass custom themes
description:
I am creating an rmarkdown template that is styled via a function that wraps `flex_dashboard`. The documentation for `flex_dashboard` states that you must provide a string naming one of the bootstrap themes and doesn't discuss how to provide a custom theme. After a lot of tinkering, I found that providing theme arguments must be specified as a `list` and not a `bs_theme` object. Would be nice to have this documented in the package.  

```
my_flexdash_themer <- function(bg, fg, primary, secondary, version, ...){

    my_theme <- list(bg = bg,
                                    fg = fg,
                                    primary = primary,
                                    secondary = secondary,
                                    version = version)

  flexdashboard::flex_dashboard(
                                theme = my_theme,
                                ...)
}

```
### Yaml for Rmarkdown
```
---
title: "Template Title"
output: 
  mypackage::my_flexdash_themer
---
```

title: `bslib` stylesheet overrides do not work with `shiny_prerendered` and `rmarkdown` `2.8`
description:
## Problem
Referencing stylesheets in the front matter will not override the Bootstrap theme with flexdashboard and `runtime: shiny_prerendered`. This only appears to be an issue in `rmarkdown` `2.8`.

```rmarkdown
---
output:
  flexdashboard::flex_dashboard:
    css:
      - mystyle.css
```

## Background
[`bslib` allows for style overrides](https://rstudio.github.io/bslib/articles/bslib.html#add-rules) by specifying stylesheets in the `css` property in the front matter. This works when rendering `html_document`s (both `shiny` and `shiny_prerendered`). It also works in `flexdashboard` when using `runtime: shiny`, but not with `runtime: shiny_prerendered`.

<details>
<summary>
📸  Expand for visual examples of each
</summary>

### `html_document` + `runtime: shiny`

![Screen Shot 2021-06-08 at 1 58 34 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/448744/121242891-138d1100-c86b-11eb-90ed-7d8b105b1676.png)

### `html_document` + `runtime: shiny_prerendered`

![Screen Shot 2021-06-08 at 1 58 59 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/448744/121242958-256eb400-c86b-11eb-9c9d-c342f5c1b255.png)

### `flexdashboard::flex_dashboard` + `runtime: shiny`

![Screen Shot 2021-06-08 at 1 59 19 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/448744/121243044-446d4600-c86b-11eb-887a-e36338029029.png)

### `flexdashboard::flex_dashboard` + `runtime: shiny_prerendered`

![Screen Shot 2021-06-08 at 1 59 45 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/448744/121243068-4cc58100-c86b-11eb-9f50-a6b8b4eca318.png)
</details>

It appears that the theme CSS (`cosmo` in this example) is applied _after_ the prerendered HTML is loaded, thus overriding the added rules (`nes`).
![Screen Shot 2021-06-08 at 3 01 23 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/448744/121242694-dc1e6480-c86a-11eb-943b-56cbaf5f86a6.png)
![Screen Shot 2021-06-08 at 3 00 28 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/448744/121242708-df195500-c86a-11eb-8f7c-a2cb8c4ebce5.png)

## Steps to reproduce
1. Install `rmarkdown` `2.8` (latest version)
2. Create an RMarkdown document with the following code
```rmarkdown
---
title: "bslib css overrides"
runtime: shiny_prerendered
output:
  flexdashboard::flex_dashboard:
    css:
      - https://unpkg.com/nes.css@latest/css/nes.min.css
---
```{r, context="server"}
print("Hello World")
``` #end
```
2. Note the NES stylesheet changes the cursor, but the default `cosmo` theme overrides the font, for example.

title: Suddenly cannot use thematic with svg devices
description:
Hello,

I have a dashboard for which I have been using the svg device for plots and thematic for automatic theming of the plots. It has worked fine but between the last generation of the dashboard (11th May) and now, something has broken. I've tried rolling back package versions of flexdashboard, knitr, thematic, bslib, ggplot2, but I can't seem to find the culprit.

Here's an MWE illustrating the problem:
``` r
    ---
    title: "Untitled" 
    output: 
      flexdashboard::flex_dashboard:
        theme:
          bootswatch: cosmo
          base_font:
            google: Open Sans
        orientation: columns
        vertical_layout: fill
    ---

    ```{r setup, include=FALSE}
    knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, dev = "svg")
    library(flexdashboard)
    library(ggplot2)
    library(thematic)
    thematic_rmd(font = "auto")
    ```

    ### Chart A

    ```{r}
    ggplot(iris, (aes(Sepal.Width, Sepal.Length))) +
      geom_point()
    ```
```

This will cause knitr compilation to hang. But if you comment out either the knitr line that set the device as svg (or change it to png) **or** the thematic_rmd call, then it will compile perfectly fine. So there must be some recent change that means thematic doesn't play well with svg devices.

title: Accessibility issues
description:
Hi,

The flexdashboard has a few accessibility issues (see Wave results for one of the examples https://wave.webaim.org/report#/https://beta.rstudioconnect.com/jjallaire/htmlwidgets-highcharter/htmlwidgets-highcharter.html) in the default HTML that I think should be addressed:

* In the examples include `lang=en` in the markdown so that 'Language missing or invalid' is taken care of. This one the user can fix in their own markdown files.
* Contrast can be fixed using custom CSS.
* The empty button and links for the menu should be handled in JavaScript as it is harder for the user to modify. I see that for the social menu on mobile the word 'Share' appears. That can be modified to have 'Share' be hidden on desktop and visible on mobile.
* The aria-label `role=menu` can be fixed by defining `role=menuitem` for the links in the menu.

I will try to share a pull request but wanted to note down the issues.

Let me know if you have any questions or suggestions.

library(shiny)

  actionButton(inputId = "button", label = "Re-render"),
  gaugeOutput(outputId = "gauge")
)

server <- function(input, output) {
  
  observeEvent(input$button, ignoreNULL = FALSE, {

    output$gauge <- renderGauge(
      gauge(
        value = sample(1:10, size = 1),
        min = sample(1:5, size = 1),
        max = sample(6:10, size = 1),
        symbol = sample(c("%", "$", "#"), size = 1),
        label = round(runif(1), 5)

}

title: renderDT() with DT.fillContainer option being set to TRUE
description: When using flexdashboard with DT tables, the DT table will be vertically filled automatically, thanks to the following lines : https://github.com/rstudio/flexdashboard/blob/6ad5aceb16b07850535786c45a0e55f114f4d2d7/R/flex_dashboard.R#L189-L194 However, this magic only works for a static DT table, i.e., the table generated by `DT::datatable()` directly. If the table is generated by `DT::renderDT()`, i.e., on the shiny runtime, `DT.fillContainer` option won't be set to `TRUE` and the table rendered may be displayed in an undesired style, when the container's height is limited. What's worse is, users can't even view the hidden data rows, since there's no Y-scroller. It's very confused to the user and it's difficult to know that this can be resolved by providing the `fillContainer = TRUE` to the `DT::datatable()` call. Since FlexDashboard has already does this magic (rendering DT table with `DT.fillContainer` option being set to `TRUE`) to the static DT, I'm asking the question that : 1. Can FlexDashboard render a reactive DT table (shiny runtime) with `DT.fillContainer` option being set to `TRUE`, automatically? 1. If not, is it possible to do it in DT? I mean, is it possible for DT to know that it's rendering within a FlexDashboard? Thanks! (Ref to https://github.com/rstudio/DT/issues/818) ### An Example to illustrate what I say (See the comment on the sidebar) ``````Rmd --- title: "Test Flexboard Shiny App" runtime: shiny output: flexdashboard::flex_dashboard: orientation: columns vertical_layout: fill --- ```{r setup, include=FALSE} library(flexdashboard) library(shiny) library(DT) ``` Sidebar {.sidebar} ----------------------------------------------------------------------- Please pay attention to the scrollY bar of each table. - The 2nd table's scroll bar can't be displayed but the 1st and 3rd can. - The reason is that DT table need `fillContainer` to be set to `TRUE` in order to display correctly. - FlexDashboard is able to enable this option for static DT table but not for DT in Shiny mode. Column Data ----------------------------------------------------------------------- ### 1. shiny - fillContainer = TRUE ```{r} DT::renderDT(DT::datatable( mtcars, fillContainer = TRUE )) ``` ### 2. shiny - no fillContainer ```{r} DT::renderDT(DT::datatable( mtcars )) ``` ### 3. static - no fillContainer ```{r} DT::datatable( mtcars ) ``` ``````

title: New pkgdown documentation site - new build plan?
description:
Hi @rich-iannone  @schloerke and @jjallaire -

As discussed, we'll convert this R Markdown documentation website into a pkgdown site. I see that the current site is in the `gh-pages` branch, so I wanted to check in before throwing a new documentation site in the mix. Many of our teams prefer not to have the pkgdown `docs` living in the `master` branch, but I don't see any Travis or GitHub Actions for the package build in this repo.

What we did for the [R Markdown documentation site](https://rmarkdown.rstudio.com/docs/) was use Travis to build the site and deploy to Netlify. See code here:

https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/284b685c2feb68083b3434c6ca38717cd61cbeea/.travis.yml#L29-L37

I believe we can do the same combo of Travis + Netlify, or Travis + GH pages if you prefer.

Another option, adopted by the tidyverse team, is using GitHub Actions to deploy to the `gh-pages` branch (then use either GH pages or Netlify to publish), following [`usethis::use_tidy_github_actions`](https://usethis.r-lib.org/reference/tidyverse.html). For example:
+ https://github.com/allisonhorst/palmerpenguins/blob/master/.github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml
+ https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml


Do any of these solutions sound preferable to you all?

title: Release flexdashboard 0.5.2

- [x] If not a new package, make sure any warnings/errors in CRAN check results page are fixed

- [x] Create a GitHub issue called "Release checklist for [version]". Include the steps below as checklist steps.

- [x] Create branch labelled `v[version]-rc`, for example, `v1.5.2-rc` (the `"rc"` stands for "Release Candidate").

- [x] Change the DESCRIPTION and NEWS on this branch to change the version number to the desired version for CRAN, e.g. from `1.5.1.9008` to `1.5.2`.

- [x] Commit and push to the RC branch.

- [x] Clean your package directory to remove any extraneous files, including ones that are git-ignored. (Warning, this will delete any unsaved buffers in RStudio! Also, be sure to close RStudio before taking this step!) Use `git clean -xdf`.

- [x] Build your package with:
`PATH=$PATH:/Applications/RStudio.app/Contents/MacOS/pandoc R CMD build [pkgdir]`

- [x] Do a sanity check by installing/testing the built package.

- [x] Perform revdep check using `https://github.com/r-lib/revdepcheck`, if this is not the initial CRAN release.

- [x] Run `R CMD check --as-cran pkg_version.tar.gz` both locally and on win-builder. You can also use https://r-hub.github.io/rhub/.

- [x] Read every bullet point in the CRAN Policies document if this is the first release of the package. Be sure to print it out and check off the items one by one.

- [x] Submit to CRAN via their online form at `https://cran.r-project.org/submit.html`

- [x] If there are R CMD check warnings that are unavoidable, make sure to explain them in the comments.

- [x] If rejected, make changes on the RC branch and bump the fourth (patch) version component (i.e. `1.5.2.1`)

- [ ] When accepted, tag the RC branch with a `v1.5.2.1` tag (or whatever version you finally ended up getting accepted), and push the tag to `origin`.

This leads to them being put inside `chart-shim` wrappers which cause long tables to be cut off. 

I think this is a more general problem with the way `flexdashboard` decides what sort of container to put content in, because I've noticed the same thing happen when I generate custom HTML content for a section with `htmltools`. 

An example is when I tried to put an image and a guage in the same section:

    div(

       div(class = "rage-guage-guage",

           gaugeSectors(success = c(0.25, 1), warning = c(-0.25, 0.25), danger = c(-0.25, -1))

    )
    ))

It would be useful if there was some way to force a row/column section to behave in a fixed manner rather than relying on its guesswork. Perhaps something like being able to do:

description:

I was wondering what is the recommended way to proceed with such use-case.

The code below is a simple dashboard with a table (using formattable) that is first loaded with a dataset. The user can use the file upload widget to upload a new dataset - I would like to understand how to refresh the table once the upload is complete. Should this be done in the new_df_tbl event?

The example is self-contained and can be used directly in Rstudio.

    ---
    title: "Basic"
    output: 
      flexdashboard::flex_dashboard:
        orientation: rows
        vertical_layout: fill
    runtime: shiny
    ---
    
    ```{r setup, include=FALSE}
    library(flexdashboard)
    library(shinyWidgets)
    library(shiny)
    library(formattable)
    library(tidyverse)
    ```
    
    ```{r}
    df <- data.frame(
      x = rnorm(100),
      y = rnorm(100)
    )
    ```
    
    ```{r}
    df_tbl <- reactive({
        df %>% select(x, y) # do some stuff here but for simplicity we do nothing
    })
    ```

    =======================================================================
    
    ```{r}
    fileInput("file1", "Choose CSV File",
                    multiple = FALSE,
                    accept = c("text/csv",
                             "text/comma-separated-values,text/plain",
                             ".csv"))
    
    br()
    
    actionButton(inputId = "apply", label = "Apply", icon = icon("play"))

    ```{r}
    rv <- reactiveValues(data = NULL)
    rv <- df
    
    observeEvent(eventExpr = input$apply, 
      handlerExpr = {
          req(input$file1)
          file <- read_csv(input$file1$datapath)
          rv$data <- file
      }, ignoreNULL = FALSE)
    ```
    
    
    Main
    =======================================================================

      formattable(df_tbl())
    })

title: Reactive UI takes up entire column when used outside of sidebar
facebook social share -- proposed fix
description:
The default social share for facebook currently doesn't work. 

To reproduce, visit any example flexdashboard online ([such as this one](https://beta.rstudioconnect.com/jjallaire/htmlwidgets-d3heatmap/htmlwidgets-d3heatmap.html)) and attempt to share via Facebook.

Digging into the HTML reveals that the request sent to facebook is:

```
https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?s=100&p[url]="+encodeURIComponent(location.href)
```

Changing it to the following solves this issue:
```
https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u="+encodeURIComponent(location.href)
```

title: pandoc template use pagetitle variable instead of title variable as main header
description:
An issue has been open on the [community](https://community.rstudio.com/t/use-r-object-in-title-of-flexdashboard/35847) about a difference of behavioir between `html_document` and `flex_dashboard` on a very specific feature: the hability to dynamically change the title This does not works ```` --- output: flexdashboard::flex_dashboard --- ```{r setup, include=FALSE} library(flexdashboard) my_title <- "I am the title" ``` --- title: '`r my_title`' --- Test R Markdown flexdashboard ```` but this works ```` --- output: html_document --- ```{r setup, include=FALSE} my_title <- "I am the title" ``` --- title: '`r my_title`' --- Test R Markdown HTML ```` First part in behavior difference is that `flexdashboard` pandoc template does not use `title` for its main header, but `pagetitle`. https://github.com/rstudio/flexdashboard/blob/ccb5f1ad057f42da24818d6ff3acb0f4e6b944cb/inst/rmarkdown/templates/flex_dashboard/resources/default.html#L68-L69 Whereas in `html_document` https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/5fae36eb42318534880760398cc86067558008c5/inst/rmd/h/default.html#L491-L493 ```html $if(title)$

$title$

``` For consistency, it could be better to use `title` instead of `pagetitle` ? This issue also appears because there is a special case here where when no title is provided, rmarkdown enforces a `pagetitle` value by command argument to prevent a warning. This command flag overwrite anything set in the document. I'll also open an issue in Rmarkdown about that to be less strict in this case to be able to use the pandoc feature of defining metadata in several yaml chunks. Thanks

title: change gauge min/max labels and add threshold indicator

Also, I would like to add an indicator such as a black line on the gauge that indicates a certain threshold for average population risk. 

I haven't found a way to do either of these things within the standard gauge parameters, and am wondering if there's a way to customize/access the widget itself to make these changes if not possible the standard way.

build_gauge <- function(value, average_risk) {
  return(gauge(round(value, 2), symbol = "%", min = 0, max = 1, sectors = gaugeSectors(success = c(0, average_risk), warning = c(average_risk, average_risk*2), danger = c(average_risk*2, 100)), abbreviate = TRUE, abbreviateDecimals = 0))

Font Awesome displays square in valueBox
description: Related to issue #203, but in `valueBox`. Some icons display correctly in valueBox, setting the icon with the `icon` argument, but others are not found and display as a backup icon (square box). If the `icon` argument is set to a value that starts with 'fa-', the first word in the class is also 'fa', but sometimes it needs to be set to other values such as 'fas' to display properly. Example of failure: `valueBox('hello', icon = "fa-tachometer-alt")` Output as displayed after js processing: `` (shows as square) Example of workaround: `valueBox('hello', icon = "- fas fa-tachometer-alt")` Output as displayed after js processing: `` (shows as correct icon) The workaround relies on flexdashboard.js splitting the iconLib on `-` (around line 1680) and interpretation of the resulting tag being sufficiently tolerant, but there probably should be a mechanism just to specify that full class.

title: Bug in `downloadButton` with `downloadHandler` explicitly assigned to output slot
description:
This report is for two separate, but related issues. 

In `flexdashboard` the `downloadButton()` doesn't seem to behave as documented. There are two issues that I could identify: 
1. When used as per the documentation (`?downloadButton`), with the `downloadHandler()` explicitly assigned to an `output` slot, the download button doesn't render at all. 
2. When defining the `downloadHandler()` anonymously, the download button will render, but it's label will be hardcoded to `Download`, as it seems to ignore custom labels. 

None of these issues seem to affect the Download Link, which both renders as expected and takes into account a custom label.

Here's a minimum reproducible example. 

    ---
    title: "Bug with download button"
    output:
        flexdashboard::flex_dashboard:
        orientation: columns

title: `source_code` GitHub links needs to use `target="_blank"` when used in an `iframe`, such as in Connect
description:
GitHub uses a [frame-ancestors Content Security Policy directive](https://githubengineering.com/githubs-csp-journey/#frame-ancestors) so it cannot be embedded inside an iframe. As a result when clicking on these links inside the connect iframe you e.g. the following error in the JS console.

> Refused to display 'https://github.com/jimhester/tidyversedashboard' in a frame because an ancestor violates the following Content Security Policy directive: "frame-ancestors 'none'".

The workaround for this is to use the [`target="_blank"` attribute](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/a#attr-target) in the anchor element to force them to be opened in a new window.

An example connect app that exhibits this behavior is https://connect.rstudioservices.com/connect/#/apps/91/access/35

", some_other_line) htmltools::HTML(to_print) }) ``` ```` scroll bar (as determined by the css styling line) will no longer work I would be grateful if (a) renderText({ ... }) would actually produce a scrollbar automatically when the text was too long, or somehow the above problem would be fixed. title: All apps with htmlwidgets failing to render on Mac after #150
description:
I think that #150 unfortunately introduced one bug, that I can't quite figure out why. I've found that this fix works fine for apps with no htmlwidgets, but it fails to render in all other circumstances (DT, ggplotly, d3heatmap, ...). (Going back just one commit to 73a7fe1dd6644b6f63e311fbcf41bc361266a1fe fixes the issue; of course, then you get the terrible #149 Pandoc bug). Here's a repro (the first example in the [website](http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com/flexdashboard/examples.html)): ````r --- title: "NBA Scoring (2008)" output: flexdashboard::flex_dashboard: orientation: rows social: menu source_code: embed --- ```{r setup, include=FALSE} library(knitr) library(d3heatmap) library(flexdashboard) url <- "http://datasets.flowingdata.com/ppg2008.csv" nba_players <- read.csv(url, row.names = 1) ``` ### Stats by Player {data-width=650} ```{r} d3heatmap(nba_players, scale = "column") ``` ### Top Scorers {data-width=350} ```{r} knitr::kable(nba_players[1:20,c("G", "MIN", "PTS")]) ``` ```` Here's what it should look like: ![screen shot 2017-11-16 at 11 30 42 pm](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6527540/32921649-4872d1ac-cb26-11e7-9187-3a5321dd743a.png) Here's what it looks like at commit 73a7fe1dd6644b6f63e311fbcf41bc361266a1fe (ugly, because of #149 ): ![screen shot 2017-11-16 at 11 31 00 pm](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6527540/32921773-c241229a-cb26-11e7-9c44-b97b3305b69b.png) If we go one commit forward to Yihui's fix (to c90540f7acd686ea67fc7ba3f5f36cfb870da8c5), the rendering fails with get the following output: ``` processing file: NBA-scoring-with-d3heatmap.Rmd |......... | 14% ordinary text without R code |................... | 29% label: setup (with options) List of 1 $ include: logi FALSE |............................ | 43% ordinary text without R code |..................................... | 57% label: unnamed-chunk-1 Quitting from lines 22-23 (NBA-scoring-with-d3heatmap.Rmd) Error in switch(options$dev, pdf = ".pdf", jpeg = ".jpeg", ".png") : EXPR must be a length 1 vector Calls: ... fun -> withVisible -> knit_print -> html_screenshot Execution halted ``` I've tried other apps, and the only common denominator in the problematic chunks is that it is creating an htmlwidget.

title: Flexdashboard and Plotly interaction causes issues with scrollbar on legend of Plotly graphs
description:
Someone else asked this question on stackoverflow, but I am having the same problem. https://stackoverflow.com/questions/46495164/flexdashboard-plotly-interaction-results-in-odd-scroll-bar-behavior

Basically when I have multiple plotly plots within a flexdashboard, the first plot doesn't have a scroll bar, but any subsequent plots are getting a scrollbar that I cannot remove. 

According to the response to the stackoverflow question "flexdashboard is the culprit in this case because of how it is dynamically fitting the available space and informing plotly.js on how to render. It is worth noting this appears as SVG in the source html."

title: renderValueBox doesn't show values
description:
If you wrap `valueBox` within `renderValueBox` then the valueBox won't show values correctly.

Run this snippet once....and you'll see the value box show up correctly. Then "Run Document" (within RStudio) a 2nd time and you won't see the values anymore (looks like it only shows the values right after the Rmd compiles)

NOTE: Make sure to replace the `'''` I put in with three backticks (since i'm trying to show md code within a md)

```
---
title: "Untitled"
output: 
  flexdashboard::flex_dashboard:
    orientation: columns
    runtime: shiny
---

'''{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(flexdashboard)
'''

'''{r}
renderValueBox(valueBox(value = 10,
                        icon = "fa-dollar",
                        color = "primary"))

'''
```

The fix is: Don't put your valueBoxes within `renderValueBox`....but I wanted to report this anyway in case it's truly a bug.

I have a project made of `index.Rmd`, `child.Rmd` and `grandchild.Rmd` (in the same directory).

`index.Rmd` contains:

and `grandchild.Rmd` contains:

When trying to compile `index.Rmd` (CTRL+SHIFT+K in RStudio Server) the compilation  fails with error (in the Rmarkdown tab in RStudio):

title: Controlling visibility of navbar menu items
description:
I'm using Shinyproxy to provide authenthication to some Shiny applications that use flexdashboards. While it is easy to implement basic authorisation in R code blocks to limit access to certain functionality and also hide most of the corresponding UI, I'm having some difficulties with hiding page links in the navbar. 

Just to be clear, I'm not trying to hide the menu item as a way to secure the application, the functionalities to create or retrieve data and generate output are secured server side.  

Using the {.hidden} mechanism makes the link invisible to all users. Since it isn't possible (I could be wrong here) to render the navbar from a reactive context with flexdashboard, the easiest way to hide this would be through manipulating the class attribute through a javascript event listener. This listener can be added based on the users permissions. 

However It is cumbersome to target specific items from the menu item with javascript as they don't have id's. In order to hide a list item, you would have to use a selector that takes into account that it is a grandchild of the navbar element which has a child with a specific href attribute.  It would be easier if the list item elements had an assigned ID, maybe something like `<li id="navbar-item-section-title>`. 

It could be I've missed something obvious here, in which case you have my sincere apologies and my gratitude for pointing me in the right direction.

title: Linkable valueBox "remembers" previous links
description:
I use `valueBox` to dynamically create links based on user input. When the dashboard first launches, everything works as expected. Clicking on the value box opens the link. However, when I change the input and click on the value box again, it opens two tabs, one for the old link and one for the new link. If I change the input again, clicking the value box would open three tabs. It appears that somehow the value box "remembers" all previous links and open all of them when clicked.

Here is a minimum example. I comment out the code so that GitHub doesn't try to render the markdown.

```
# ---
# title: "Test Linkable valueBox"
# output: 
#   flexdashboard::flex_dashboard:
#     orientation: rows
# runtime: shiny
# ---
# 
# ```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# library(flexdashboard)
# ```
# 
# Sidebar {.sidebar}
# =======================================================================
# 
# ```{r}
# textInput("website", "Website", "http://google.com")
# ```
# 
# Dashboard
# =======================================================================
# 
# Row
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 
# ### valueBox {.value-box}
# 
# ```{r}
# renderValueBox({
#   valueBox(value = input$website, href = input$website)

title: read_chunks with shiny not working
description:
Hi there. First of all, many many thanks for this wonderful package. I'm using it extensively in my day-to-day work.

The situation: to properly organize the source code of a large shiny-based flexdashboard (multipage, lots of info), I decided to follow the instructions detailed in this [webpage](http://zevross.com/blog/2014/07/09/making-use-of-external-r-code-in-knitr-and-r-markdown/).

I put the source code of three dropdown selectors in an external R script. In brief, these three selectors are linked hierarchically, i.e. the first selector contains an initial list, and then when you choose one of the options, the second selector reacts populating its values, and same for the third one.

Then, I "embed" the code be using the `read_chunk` function from the `knitr` package and the `<< x >>`, naming the code chunk with the value in the external script, or even using the `code=readLines(xxx)`. In all cases, when I run the dashboard, what I see is that the first selector if properly populated (as it is statically populated from at the start of the execution), but the other two selectors do not react to the selection of the first one.

Not sure if its is bug or I'm doing something wrong. Any help will be appreciated.

Juan,

PS: I guess that for organization purposes, I'm alligned with requests #81 or #82, but I'm not sure about the status of these features or if they will solve my problem.

title: [Feature Request]Add support for unicode characters in page title?
description:
Currently, if a page title consists of unicode characters, page link will not work as advertised:

```
示例
=====================================
```

The actual link to page `示例` would be determined by the number of components that came before it, it seems. Eg. `#dashboard-13`. Page linking is still possible but tedious: you have build the page, get the element id in the HTML, then go back to code and set href to it.

To allow page linking in this situation, either one of the following would work:

1. Support unicode element id, so that `href = '#示例'` would just work; or
2. Allow setting custom link reference to a page. Eg.

```
示例 {data-id='examples'}
=====================================
```

would be linked to `/#example`.

title: Dynamic user inputs not rendering in local browser nor on reload of browser on shiny-server
description:
[test_mtcars.txt](https://github.com/rstudio/flexdashboard/files/769572/test_mtcars.txt)

I don't know if this question is better posed the shiny-server or r-markdown repos, but I am having a problem with the user interface dynamically updating inputs on reload of a flexdashboard. I have used `runtime: shiny` and  `runtime: shiny_prerendered` but still get the same result.

Scenario - user selects from a list of static inputs, and that static input determines the elements of another input list.  I have tried with `uiOutput("x")`/`output$x<-renderUI()` , simply `renderUI()`, and `updateSelectInput()` (with `observe`) methods - all with the same result.  A reactive selection of input choices based on the initial selection feeds those methods. The methods all work fine in a traditionally styled Shiny App.

With rmarkdown and flexdashboard, the document renders fine with Rstudio, but when deployed on shiny-server after a render, it does not load the dynamic user inputs.

I've traced the websocket messages in the console for a successful load and for a non-successful load - it appears that the dynamic outputs are just not getting called/invalidated upon reload of the .Rmd document.

If I make a change to the .Rmd file in RStudio server, save it, and then reload from shiny-server in the browser it works the first time. But, if I re-load the file, it does not update the dynamic inputs (and hence  the application hangs).

This makes me think it is an issue with r-markdown and some form of caching, as it renders ok initially or when the render is forced (as in RStudio).

I will post a code example to illustrate this behavior, but I can't find a lot of information on dynamic inputs with flexdashboard and Rmarkdown on shiny-server. Using latest CRAN versions of Rmarkdown, Rstudio, shiny, flexdashboard and shiny-server. Will test with RStudio Connect once I get that up and running.

I attached a text file with a simple rmarkdown/flexdashboard non-working example (when opened from Rstudio browser with "Open in Browser") if local, or on shiny-server (test_mtcars.txt).

Regards,
Jason

title: Align multiple valueboxes/gauges counter to overall orientation
description:
At the moment, because the overall orientation is either columns _or_ rows, it is currently impossible to align multiple valueboxes or gauges next to each other in column layout or above each other in row layout. Simple layouts can usually be translated, but even mildly complicated layouts are impossible:

``````

---
title: "Untitled"
output: 
  flexdashboard::flex_dashboard:
    orientation: columns
    vertical_layout: fill

---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(flexdashboard)
```

Left column {.sidebar data-width=300}
----------------------------------------------------------------------

### Left sidebar

```{r}
mtcars[, 1:2]
```

Center column
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### Box 1

```{r}
valueBox('left please')
```

### Box 2 

```{r}
valueBox('right please')
```

### Center chart

```{r}
plot(1)
```


Right column {data-width=300}
----------------

### Right column

```{r}
mtcars[, 1:2]
```
``````

which of course renders the valueboxes above each other, which looks silly if they're in the main column. It seems like adding a `data-width` parameter to the `h3` header of each or setting the `fig.width`/`fig.align` chunk options should flow them together as screen width allows, but it doesn't.

Thus, is it possible to add
- the option to set individual flexbox widths (as a percentage of the current column, perhaps), or
- the ability to use rows within columns and vice versa, or
- a way to render mulitple valueboxes and gauges from within one code chunk?

This is related to the limitation of tabsets, which can't contain more than a single figure, and are thus useless for valueboxes and gauges. Maybe it's time to break into `h4` headers.

title: Resizing with server-side rendered objects kills entire dashboard

I'm trying to port over my shinydashboards to flexdashboard and I'm running into issues with objects that are rendered server-side.

In this example, I have an input selector that is rendered server-side

```
output$weeklyWeekSelector <- renderUI({
    selectInput('weeklyWeeks',
                label = 'Uker',
                choices = as.list(weeks),
                multiple=TRUE,selectize=FALSE,
                selected = weeks[1:26],
                size=35)
  })
```

and then displayed on the dashboard:

```
uiOutput("weeklyWeekSelector")
```

This works well the first time I load the page, however, if I do the following:

This issue also arises when I render a ggvis plot server-side and pass it through.

This issue arrises when I use both:
